title: TokenizationRules

operations.decimalization: Changes representational precision or quantity granularity.
operations.fractionalization: Expresses divisible units, participations or rights.
operations.tokenization: Creates a digital representation referencing a qualified governed object, right or value.
operations.minting: Creates an ecosystem-recognized representation or issuance after applicable eligibility, authority, provenance and policy gates.
operations.decentralization: Distributes control, validation, execution or governance across independently authorized participants or infrastructure.
operations.democratization: Broadens access or participation under explicit eligibility and authority rules.

rules: Underlying governed object, right or value remains primary.
A token cannot manufacture ownership or authority.
Tokenization, minting, decimalization and fractionalization are distinct operations.
Physical asset backing is required only where the underlying object/right contract or applicable jurisdiction requires it; it is not a universal tokenization rule.
Proof-of-utility is an optional domain qualification unless a higher-authority contract requires it.
Democratized issuance remains subject to authority, eligibility, jurisdiction, consent and policy gates.
Transfers must pass identity, authority, eligibility, policy and settlement gates.
Supply and fractional-unit calculations must be deterministic and auditable.
Revocation and recovery preserve provenance and the underlying rights record.
